scope.description: Bounded, deterministic probe of whether a lost follower Accepted reply is repaired by the protocol's own resend/retry machinery within a window of 100 resend periods, or only by an unrelated later proposal.
assumptions: 2-node cluster so the write quorum is the leader's own acceptance plus exactly one follower receipt: one dropped message is enough to hide the quorum from the leader
error-free memory storage, FIFO delivery of everything else, no reordering, no crash and no leadership change during the window
one logical step per node equals one tick(), so the 500-step window contains 100 of the configured 5-tick resend periods for both roles

experiment.prefix: Deterministic in-process simulation of the core crate: two real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2; configuration_id 1; MemoryStorage; error-free storage) built by OmniPaxosConfig::build, never run concurrently - the harness drives them manually: each step calls tick() on both, drains take_outgoing_messages() into a FIFO, and delivers every message to the receiver's handle_incoming, except that it deliberately discards exactly one PaxosMsg::Accepted (the follower's receipt). Node 1 has leader_priority 1 so the election is deterministic; election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1. Case lost_accepted_leaves_entry_undecided: elect (both nodes Leader/Follower in the accept phase), append one entry at the leader, drop the follower's Accepted, then run 100 resend periods of ticks (500 steps) with everything else delivered; it emits CA_EVENT lost_accepted_window {steps,resend_periods,produced,dropped,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx,follower_accepted_idx,follower_holds_undecided_entry,leader_still_stable} and asserts exactly one Accepted was dropped, the follower really holds the entry as Undecided at index 0 with accepted_idx 1, the leader and the follower are both still at decided index 0, and the leader is still the stable leader. It then appends a second entry on the same state and emits CA_EVENT later_proposal_repairs {steps_until_decided,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx}. Case delivered_accepted_decides is the control: identical, the receipt is delivered, and the entry must be decided inside the same bounded window (CA_EVENT delivered_accepted_decides). The prerequisite the probe relies on is not 'some message was dropped' but the actual per-message operands: which message kinds were produced and which was discarded are printed in the event.
experiment.revision_reason: Compile fix only: the harness failed E0384 in the previous attempt (cannot assign to the immutable argument `drop_accepted` inside collect); the parameter is now `mut drop_accepted`. No change to the cluster, the three cases, the drop rule, the window or the asserted operands.

scope.description: Bounded probe of whether an event stream the application does not consume (bounded by RuntimeConfig::event_capacity) parks the single actor loop and withholds its command/append_notify endpoints, with a drained-stream control in the same execution.
assumptions: 3 nodes, standard majority quorum, no message loss or reordering beyond the in-process transport, all nodes run in one process on one tokio runtime

event_capacity is set to 64 so the bound is reached inside a bounded window; the source-settled mechanism (send awaits whenever the channel holds event_capacity events) does not depend on the value, only the number of unconsumed transitions does
the handle's event receiver exists from construction, so an application that never subscribes still leaves it unread
excluded: proving the cluster-wide outage (quorum loss) at the 1024 default capacity
schedule independence and any rate bound on how quickly the bound is reached

basis.prefix: Three real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2,3) are built with OmniPaxosConfig::build over omnipaxos_storage::memory_storage::MemoryStorage and driven by three real omnipaxos_runtime actors spawned with spawn_actor, using a harness-local `TestRuntime` (tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; the crate's TokioRuntime behind the tokio_runtime feature is not required). An in-process transport task per node forwards every message from that node's `outgoing_messages()` to the receiver returned by `msg.get_receiver()`. RuntimeConfig: tick_period 2ms, egress_period 1ms, event_capacity 64, append_notify_timeout 1500ms; ServerConfig: election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1, flush_batch_tick_timeout 100. Proposals are paced at 4ms so consecutive decided-index changes are observed in separate ticks (a burst would decide many entries inside one tick gap and produce a single amalgamated event). Case `unconsumed_event_stream_stops_actor_loop` leaves each node's event receiver unread (the handle always owns one after spawn_actor; the application never calls subscribe_events or never reads it) while ordinary appends keep the cluster busy until all three event channels are full; case `drained_event_stream_keeps_actor_loop_running` is the same cluster, capacity and activity with one difference: a task per node drains the event stream. The decisive evidence of case 1 is (a) all three event channels full with a live (not closed) receiver, (b) at least one node whose actor never answers a `decided_idx` command again across ten 200ms samples, (c) that parked node's `append_notify_with_timeout(.., 300ms)` not resolving inside 4s although the actor that would produce its Timeout runs on that same tick path; the assertion messages print the observed channel state. Case 2 requires every node to keep answering and a fresh append_notify from a follower to resolve Ok(idx>=1).

scope.description: Bounded, deterministic probe of whether a lost follower Accepted reply is repaired by the protocol's own resend/retry machinery within a window of 100 resend periods, or only by an unrelated later proposal.
assumptions: 2-node cluster so the write quorum is the leader's own acceptance plus exactly one follower receipt: one dropped message is enough to hide the quorum from the leader
error-free memory storage, FIFO delivery of everything else, no reordering, no crash and no leadership change during the window
one logical step per node equals one tick(), so the 500-step window contains 100 of the configured 5-tick resend periods for both roles

basis.prefix: Deterministic in-process simulation of the core crate: two real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2; configuration_id 1; MemoryStorage; error-free storage) built by OmniPaxosConfig::build, never run concurrently - the harness drives them manually: each step calls tick() on both, drains take_outgoing_messages() into a FIFO, and delivers every message to the receiver's handle_incoming, except that it deliberately discards exactly one PaxosMsg::Accepted (the follower's receipt). Node 1 has leader_priority 1 so the election is deterministic; election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1. Case lost_accepted_leaves_entry_undecided: elect (both nodes Leader/Follower in the accept phase), append one entry at the leader, drop the follower's Accepted, then run 100 resend periods of ticks (500 steps) with everything else delivered; it emits CA_EVENT lost_accepted_window {steps,resend_periods,produced,dropped,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx,follower_accepted_idx,follower_holds_undecided_entry,leader_still_stable} and asserts exactly one Accepted was dropped, the follower really holds the entry as Undecided at index 0 with accepted_idx 1, the leader and the follower are both still at decided index 0, and the leader is still the stable leader. It then appends a second entry on the same state and emits CA_EVENT later_proposal_repairs {steps_until_decided,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx}. Case delivered_accepted_decides is the control: identical, the receipt is delivered, and the entry must be decided inside the same bounded window (CA_EVENT delivered_accepted_decides). The prerequisite the probe relies on is not 'some message was dropped' but the actual per-message operands: which message kinds were produced and which was discarded are printed in the event.
